name: clinical_v0_gate167_tail
rationale: Composed final-layer weights identify units 198 and 38 as positive readout paths that activate for high normalized values. In 128 calibration patients, their active cases remain underestimated after the original affine correction; almost all are measured variables rather than static/administrative channels. Increase only these two effective output coefficients by 1%, a fixed conservative expansion of the existing learned paths. Negative GELU-tail contributions change in the opposite direction, also consistent with the common positive offset in the low/middle range. No fitting, gradients, optimizer or test data. Exact median-draw activations of the edited model show unit 198 still underestimating in its positive intermediate range (median normalized errors -0.0128, -0.0327, -0.0492 in activation bins 0-0.5, 0.5-1, 1-2), across 93, 81, 96 calibration patients. Above 2 the median error reverses sign to +0.0223. Add a localized triangular correction in preactivation z198: k*(GELU(16*z)-4*GELU(16*(z-1.5))+3*GELU(16*(z-2)))/16, k=0.04*the current effective coefficient. It rises toward the strongest intermediate underestimation and switches off before the high tail. A single fixed 4% slope is used; no fitting or sweep. Reuse three existing neurons with negligible effective contributions. Unit 38 is unchanged because its remaining residual signs are inconsistent. The running benchmark candidate remains unchanged; no clinical test result informed this proposal. Compose the independent 1% sharpening of negative-only head unit 47, using its already specified weights unchanged. The local positive repair reduced mean confirmation MSE but cost MAE; unit 47 sharpening reduced MAE on both confirmation seeds but slightly cost MSE. They address intermediate underestimation and a common positive negative-tail contribution through disjoint neurons. No coefficient is refitted, searched or derived from test. Test their composition as a single new hypothesis, retaining it only if full forward evaluations support joint improvement. New calibration median-draw preactivations show unit 255 remains entirely negative. Its negative coefficient turns GELU's negative lobe into a positive output hump. For z in [-1.5,-1), residual median is +0.00673; for z in [-1,-0.5), it is -0.00197, each across 127 patients. Translate this hump by changing only incoming bias 255 by -0.01. This lowers its left-tail contribution and raises its contribution near zero, unlike uniform attenuation. The pattern is stronger on static/admin/time variables; physiological subgroup signs are mixed. This is one fixed hypothesis on an experimental parent, not a demonstrated causal correction. No gradients, training, parameter sweep or test residuals are used. V1 test scores have already been seen in the ongoing benchmark; any later test is a repeated benchmark assessment. Unit167 has a negative effective output coefficient and is usually inactive. Its rare positive activation above 2 mostly denotes the hospital-admission-time variable in calibration. The original coarse bins show negative mean and median residuals in this tail on both the 128-patient composed-head diagnostic and the expanded 512-patient gate255 diagnostic; a minority of physiological cases have the opposite sign. Program two dormant units to add A*(GELU(16*(z167-2))-GELU(16*(z167-4)))/16, A=0.05*abs(coefficient167). This reduces 5% of the negative slope only between the fixed coarse bin boundaries 2 and 4, then caps the response. The existing low and negative activations are almost unaffected. The coefficient is taken directly from the weight, not fitted to residual magnitudes. Both denoising steps were probed using calibration inputs without reading targets. No gradients, optimizer, training, parameter sweep, or test-derived edit is used. Full forwards must establish whether this head-level interpretation improves accuracy. This is a separate child of gate255, not a composition with the relative-tail candidate.
